verdict.rationale: Viam documents ready-made hardware drivers pulled from its Registry and auto-initialized from config. Every camera exposes the same GetImage() method regardless of brand, and sensors and other components get the same uniform treatment, which serves as the standard interface layer. A discovery service also suggests component configurations. However, the evidence only names cameras explicitly; lidars, IMUs and GPS are never mentioned, so coverage of the story's specific sensor types is unproven. missing for 10: explicit evidence of lidar, IMU and GPS drivers or component types, documentation of the standardized data/message formats for those sensors, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a robotics engineer, I can integrate cameras, lidars, IMUs, and GPS with ready-made drivers and standard message types

citations.quote: Specify your hardware model and connection details in the config, and viam-server pulls the driver from the Registry and initializes it automatically.
Every camera component in Viam exposes the same GetImage() method regardless of brand. Same for motors, sensors, arms, and other components.
Discovery: Detect available hardware on a machine and suggest component configurations
Search by manufacturer or hardware type (for example, `webcam`, `viam:raspberry-pi:rpi5`, `viam:ufactory:xArm6`).
